chunks: Yaḥyā ibn ʿAbd Allāh Abū al-Ḥasan, Ṣāḥib al-Daylam, narrated to us; he said:
I heard Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad عليه السلام saying, while there were some people from the people of al-Kūfah in his presence:

How astonishing concerning the people: they took all of their knowledge from the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله, then acted by it and were guided, yet they think that the people of his Household did not take his knowledge—while we are the people of his Household and his progeny. In our homes the Revelation descended, and from us knowledge went out to them. Do they then think that they came to know and were guided, while we remained ignorant and went astray? Indeed, this is impossible.

key_terms.أَهْلُ بَيْتِهِ: his Household, the family of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
key_terms.الْعِلْمُ: sacred knowledge originating from the Prophet’s Household
key_terms.الْوَحْيُ: divine revelation sent down by Allah
key_terms.اهْتَدَوْا: they were guided to the right path
key_terms.رَسُولِ اللَّهِ: the Messenger of Allah, the source of divine teaching

ai.seo_question: Why does Imam Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام say that the knowledge of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم is with Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith affirms that the knowledge of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم is most rightfully found with Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام, in whose homes Revelation descended. It rejects the notion that others could possess and act upon the Prophet’s knowledge while his own Household remained ignorant of it, presenting this as an impossibility.
